1. Introduction Aitchison and Ali, 2012; Sun et al., 2012; DeCelles et al., 2014). A
traditionalviewdepictsasinglecollisionbetweenIndiaandAsiaalong

logicaleventsintheCenozoicthatraisedtheTibetanPlateauandex- Eocene(e.g.,MolnarandTapponnier,1975;PatriatandAchache,1984;
erted profound impacts on the global atmospheric circulations (e.g., YinandHarrison,2000).Subsequently,dualcollisionalprocesseswere
Molnar and Tapponnier, 1975; Dewey et al., 1988; Raymo and proposed that involved a collision of the India Plate with an in-
Ruddiman,1992;YinandHarrison,2000;Anetal.,2001;Guo,2015). traoceanic arc at ∼55Ma prior to its final collision with Asia at

bates regarding when, where, and how India and Asia collided (e.g., (Ali and Aitchison, 2005) is believed to consist of two continents,
